content: As Jensen Huang puts it, AI can help fight climate change — but only if it inflicts “an enormous amount of pain and suffering” first.   The Nvidia CEO discussed the future of energy and AI’s impact on our planet in the latest episode of The Ezra Klein Show. But his comments boil down to the same accelerationist spin we’ve seen from a variety of tech leaders as well as President Donald Trump. They promise that AI will be such a gift to humanity that it’s worth the damage caused by data centers currently running on dirty energy.  Huang’s extreme level of privilege is glaring in the interview. He’s right that there will be pain. People are already suffering from fires and floods exacerbated by climate change. People are already dying earlier because of air pollution from fossil fuels. But Huang, with a net worth of around $192.6 billion, will not pay the price of the pollution his company creates through energy-hungry chip factories and data centers. Huang tells Klein, after complaining that the US hasn’t built out enough fossil fuel plants, that: > It’s kind of like, in order to save you, they’ve got to hurt you first — that’s the nature of surgery. They’ve got to cut you open to save you. They’ve got to inflict an enormous amount of pain and suffering on you so that they can save you. And so I think AI’s kind of like that. That’s the bit that gives Thanos energy. Resources are too limited and so after disappearing half of humanity, the Marvel supervillain believes, things will be much rosier. (“I will shred this universe down to its last atom, and then create a new one, teeming with life that knows not what it has lost but only what it has been given,” he tells the Avengers.) Huang goes on to say:  > Over the next several years we have to unfortunately use fossil fuels, because we just don’t have enough sustainable energy to make a difference. And then after that, hopefully, we can transition to that. For context, nearly every country on Earth agreed to limit climate change when they adopted the Paris agreement in 2015. The accord sets a goal of cutting greenhouse gas emissions in half by 2030 and reaching net zero around 2050. That can only happen with swift transition to carbon-free energy like renewables and nuclear. Here’s just a short list of terrible things getting worse when we stall that progress to pursue advances in AI: * Earth is expected to lose 99 percent of its coral reefs. Those reefs support coastal economies, and also serve as a buffer protecting communities from tropical storms, flooding, and coastal erosion. * One in 10 people around the world, 770 million people, already face “acute risk” from sea level rise.  * Since 2001, peak daily wildfire growth rates have more than doubled in the western US. Wildfires are faster, more frequent, and more intense. These effects are showing up in Huang’s backyard, even if he’s insulated from them. He mentions in the interview that he doesn’t know what his own address is. However, he reportedly bought a $7.5 million home on Maui in 2004 — before wildfires devastated the island in 2023. That year, an Nvidia spokesperson confirmed with The Verge that the Huangs “have owned the same home in Maui for many years.” Huang’s property reportedly escaped damage, and the Nvidia spokesperson told me that the Huangs “donated significantly to local relief efforts.” But despite the philanthropy from tech billionaires with residences on Maui, the inferno also inflamed tensions over luxury properties’ hold on Maui’s water supply. “Billionaires coming to Maui, buying up large swaths of land as their, I don’t know, seventh vacation home, it’s painful for our community,” Maui County Councilmember Keani Rawlins-Fernandez told me at the time. “It underscores the stark disparity between Indigenous people who want to mālama ‘āina, care for our land, and those who see Hawaii as a vacation destination.” While greenhouse gas pollution from fossil fuels makes wildfires more dangerous by exacerbating hot, dry conditions, climate change isn’t entirely to blame for the flames that razed much of Lahaina on Maui. I reported at the time that previous generations of wealthy land grabbers primed the islands to burn. The US annexed the Kingdom of Hawaii in 1898, egged on by American plantation owners who wanted to evade import taxes. They cleared native vegetation for their businesses, allowing invasive grasses to take hold and make the landscape much more flammable than it used to be. So when I hear Huang make the case now that there will need to be sacrifices in the name of AI progress, it reminds me that we’ve seen this playbook before. An industry that wants to grow at any cost. And nearby communities and their descendants are just supposed to live with the aftermath.  Huang mentions growing community opposition to data centers in the interview with Klein, and scolds other companies for not spreading the good news with residents about how efficient data centers purportedly are before they start construction. “If they don’t want data centers to be built in their town or whatever it is, then so be it. But if you’re going to build in their town, be sure to go there and let them know what’s coming,” he says. “I am inevitable,” Thanos notoriously said — and apparently, so are AI data centers. Even so, data centers don’t actually have to be as polluting as they are turning out to be.  In the interview, Huang also (unfairly) attributes record renewable energy purchases to AI. He blames climate action for stalling the construction of energy infrastructure, presumably for fossil fuels.   > I think we just have to acknowledge that we got ourselves really gummed up in climate change and sustainable energy, and as a result, we just didn’t plan enough energy production. chineseContent: 正如黄仁勋所说，人工智能可以帮助应对气候变化——但前提是它首先造成“巨大的痛苦和磨难”。   这位 Nvidia 首席执行官在最新一集的 Ezra Klein Show 中讨论了能源的未来以及人工智能对我们星球的影响。但他的言论归根结底与我们在各种科技领袖以及唐纳德·特朗普总统身上看到的加速主义观点是一样的。他们承诺人工智能将成为人类的一份礼物，值得目前使用肮脏能源运行的数据中心所造成的损害。  黄的极端特权在采访中显而易见。他说得对，会有痛苦。人们已经在遭受因气候变化而加剧的火灾和洪水之苦。由于化石燃料造成的空气污染，人们已经提前死亡。但净资产约为 1926 亿美元的黄仁勋不会为他的公司通过高耗能芯片工厂和数据中心造成的污染付出代价。黄告诉克莱因，在抱怨美国没有建造足够的化石燃料工厂后，他说：>这有点像，为了拯救你，他们必须先伤害你——这就是手术的本质。他们必须把你切开才能救你。他们必须给你带来巨大的痛苦和折磨才能拯救你。所以我认为人工智能有点像这样。这就是赋予灭霸能量的部分。资源太有限了，所以漫威超级反派相信，在人类消失一半之后，事情会变得更加美好。 （他告诉复仇者联盟：“我将把这个宇宙撕碎成最后一个原子，然后创造一个充满生命的新宇宙，它不知道自己失去了什么，只知道自己得到了什么。”黄继续说道：> 在接下来的几年里，我们不得不不幸地
